questions.q: In the metabolism of fatty acids, beta-oxidation cleaves the carbon chain into two-carbon units. These units combine with Coenzyme A to form which molecule to enter the Krebs (TCA) cycle?
questions.explain: Beta-oxidation breaks down fatty acids into 2-carbon Acetyl CoA molecules, which then enter the Citric Acid (Krebs) Cycle for ATP production.

questions.q: Ketosis occurs when the body produces ketone bodies from Acetyl CoA. This metabolic state is primarily driven by:
options: Insufficient oxaloacetate due to low carbohydrate availability.
questions.explain: For Acetyl CoA to enter the Krebs cycle, it must condense with oxaloacetate. Oxaloacetate is derived from pyruvate (carbohydrate breakdown). If carbohydrates are low, oxaloacetate is depleted (used for gluconeogenesis), causing Acetyl CoA to be shunted into ketone production.
